analysis.title: Weekly Warm-up: Clearing Events Still Ahead
key_insights: MS says equities have been adjusting to a mid-cycle transition (peak rate of change in growth) since June. Slower Fed balance sheet growth, capital scarcity and the midterms made it worse. Several clearing events ahead should mark the end of the correction.

The quality factor has led through the transition and is now breaking out. MS says the call is now well understood and priced via positioning. Quality can still hold up if the S&P 500 trades toward the tactical downside target of 7100-7200, a slight break of the 200-day moving average.
Breadth has started to improve from narrow levels, so the index and breadth are 'meeting in the middle'. MS keeps its year-end base case of 8000 for the S&P 500.

Clearing event 1 is AI-related investor concerns: return on capital, cost and availability of capital in credit markets, safety and NIMBYism. MS expects these to come to a head over the next 3-4 weeks and says they may be a headwind until resolved.

Clearing event 2 is the midterm elections. They are typically a market headwind initially, then lead to strong 6-12 month returns. The administration has hinted at a more aggressive military stance after the election, which is now a top client concern. MS says such surprises have often been good short-term buying opportunities.

Clearing event 3 is tighter financial conditions: the Fed has begun hiking rates with limited visibility on further hikes, balance sheet growth has slowed by about half, and energy prices are higher. MS says this is on par with 2018 and almost as severe as 2022, and will likely linger into November or until the Fed pivots.

MS calls liquidity the biggest risk and the catalyst for a final low. Back-end rates have risen more than 100 bps since February. Tightening could slow growth and inflation to target, or cause market stress that forces a Fed pivot before the job is done, which would be bullish for asset prices in the short term.

Semiconductors are in the final stages of their correction. MS expects support in mid-November, about 10-15% lower, with technical support for the SOX at 9500, and expects the low to coincide with funding concerns bottoming.

About 59% of Russell 3000 stocks are down more than 20% since June 1. Semis are worst, with 96% down more than 20% and 87% down more than 30%. MS says breadth needs to improve through real buying, not just short covering as gross exposures fall.
MS's comprehensive Sentiment Indicator is only at 'Neutral'. MS expects a reading near the lows from when the Iran war began before the correction ends.

Gold and crypto have been weaker, which MS ties to Warsh's hawkish stance at Jackson Hole and the last FOMC, where the Fed raised rates by 25 bps. MS does not expect major changes in rate repricing at this week's FOMC, since front- and back-end rates have repriced about 30-40 bps lower in recent weeks.

MS expects no meaningful change in Fed balance sheet growth without more stress first. It watches SOFR spreads and bond volatility as early signs the Fed or Treasury will add liquidity. Treasury buybacks worked in March and April, and Treasury may need to increase them.

3Q26 earnings season so far: median T+1 price reaction is 0.0% absolute and +0.4% relative. The EPS surprise is 2% against a 4.4% historical average, and the sales surprise is 1.3%, in line with history. 120 of 494 S&P 500 companies have reported.

Consensus expects 3Q EPS growth of 27% and sales growth of 11% y/y. Calendar 2026 and 2027 EPS growth are 33% and 16%. Mag 7 earnings are expected to grow 32% in 3Q26 against 20% for the S&P 493, and in 2027 the S&P 493 grows 17% against 11% for the Mag 7.
S&P 500 earnings growth is skewed by unrealized gains on private AI investments (non-operating income) in 1Q/2Q26, which distort 2027 comparisons.

Short-term earnings revision breadth shows a positive spike, while FY2 breadth is +7%. Energy and Communication Services have the most positive revisions in the last 2 weeks, and Consumer Discretionary and Tech the weakest.
MS analyst previews are net +20% for KPI and NTM EPS, against +32% and +27% last quarter. Results so far are net +13% against +27% in 2Q.
MS's forecast table shows the S&P 500 at 7,624 with bear/base/bull 12-month targets of 5,900 / 8,300 / 9,400, and a current P/E of 18.6x.

MS sector ratings: Overweight Financials, Industrials, Consumer Discretionary Goods, Tech, Comm. Services, Health Care, Materials, Utilities, Consumer Services and Energy, with Staples and Real Estate Underweight (Equal Weight bucket as listed in the exhibit).

earnings_insights: 3Q26 S&P 500 EPS growth consensus est +27% y/y (blended growth rate) and sales +11.2% y/y. 120 of 494 companies (24% of companies, 26% of market cap) have reported.

3Q26 EPS surprise is 2.0% (reported vs consensus est), below the 4.4% historical average. Sales surprise is 1.3%, in line with the 1.3% historical average. The 2Q26 EPS surprise was +26%, skewed by non-operating profits from private AI investments.
Calendar 2026 EPS growth consensus est is 33% and 2027 is 16%. 2026 sales growth consensus est is 11% and 2027 is 8%.

Mag 7 net income growth consensus est is 32% in 3Q26 against 20% for the S&P 493. For 2027 the S&P 493 is expected to grow 17% against 11% for the Mag 7, largely on tough comps from one-off non-operating benefits.

Reported 3Q26 results by sector: Banks 13 of 13 reported with a -5.5% EPS surprise vs est, Information Technology 12 of 74 reported with semis EPS growth of 577%, Financials 36 of 75 reported, Industrials 24 of 80 reported.
Median T+1 price reaction is 0.0% absolute and +0.4% relative. Companies that missed both EPS and sales reacted -2.2% absolute per the exhibit, and breadth of positive reactions is 50%.

S&P 500 EBIT margin LTM is 20.1%, with consensus est of 20.6% for FY2026 and 22.7% for FY2027. LTM net margin is 15.8%, with consensus est of 16.3% for FY2026 and 17.2% for FY2027. 3Q consensus net margin is 15.7%.
Energy estimates have been revised up most since 5/31: 3Q26 EPS +128% YTD and +32.7% since 5/31. Semis are +46.5% YTD and +12.1% since 5/31 for 3Q26, and +83.4% for 2027.

MS analyst systematic results across 101 US coverage names show a net NTM EPS revision of +13%. Financials are +3% (38 results) and Industrials +9% (23 results). Consumer Discretionary is -22% and Consumer Staples is -40%.
MS analyst previews: net KPI +20% against +32% last quarter (net +34% in 2Q25), and net NTM EPS +20% against +27% last quarter.

vol_and_positioning: Hedge fund positioning has come down substantially, while retail and other passive investors remain more fully invested.
MS's comprehensive Sentiment Indicator is at 'Neutral'. MS expects it to approach the lows seen when the Iran war began before the correction ends.
The price momentum factor was heavily crowded in early-cycle stocks such as semis, which amplified the rotation.
Bond volatility has been stickier to the upside, which MS links to smaller Treasury buybacks than in March and April.
MS tracks gold and volatility as signals that money is too tight. Current gold weakness reflects a hawkish read of Warsh.
Funding markets (SOFR spreads, interbank rates) look stable. Stress there is the trigger that would force the Fed to add liquidity.
geopolitical: The war in Iran and the spike in energy prices are cited by others as drivers of inflation and higher back-end rates, while MS argues nominal GDP growth was the main driver.
The administration has floated escalating the war in Iran or another more aggressive military stance after the midterm elections, which MS says clients now see as a top risk.
Polls and Polymarket odds point to a blue wave in the midterms. A Republican Senate win or a Democratic margin of 53-55 seats would be the bigger surprise.

tension_points.bull_case: Market stress that forces the Fed or Treasury to add liquidity (balance sheet, buybacks, a larger issuance skew to the front end) would be bullish for asset prices in the short term and mark the final low.
tension_points.bear_case: Warsh treats the balance sheet as an emergency tool only and has been comfortable with tighter financial conditions. Liquidity may need to get worse before it gets better, and the Fed could stay behind the curve with more hikes priced.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Funding markets staying calm, with SOFR spreads and interbank rates not widening enough to force intervention.

tension_points.bull_case: MS sees semis in the final stages of the correction with a low in mid-November once funding concerns peak, and 96% of semis are already down more than 20% since June.
tension_points.bear_case: AI return on capital doubts and the cost and availability of capital in credit markets are not yet resolved, and semis could fall another 10-15%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A SOX break below the 9500 technical support in mid-November.
